title: Require SSO for a domain
summary: The confirmation an operator gets when turning on SSO required for students.example.edu on Lakeside University's page: what stops (email codes and passkeys for those addresses), who it reaches (31 accounts, 5 of them not yet linked), and the fail-closed consequence when the connection is down.
compare: Opened by turning the 'SSO required' switch on for a verified domain; the switch doesn't move until the dialog is confirmed. Turning it off needs no dialog.
Title asks the question with the domain in it; the body's first line says what changes and where (every product's card and Polaris Key itself).

Four bullets, one fact each with a bold lead: email codes and passkeys stop for these addresses (sessions and signed-in devices keep working); the account count; how many of them have never used the connection (they go there at their next sign-in and keep their licenses); no other way in while the connection is down.
The counts come from the server at open time (accounts with an address at the domain; how many have a link to this connection).

Buttons: Cancel (neutral, focused when the dialog opens, visible in both themes) and a primary 'Require SSO for students.example.edu' (an L1 caution confirm, not a danger button); the dialog stays open and shows the error inline if the write fails.
This is the control that replaces a product's old 'Email magic links' switch: a product that wanted SSO-only keeps it through a required domain (I-29's acceptance test).

With the dialog open the page can't scroll: on desktop the dialog is centred in the first viewport; on phone it is the console's bottom sheet (grab handle, the long primary full width above Cancel), and the page behind stays dimmed.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Dialog and drawer head (B4): a 3px rule in the origin's accent along the top (none on a destructive or cautious confirmation), a head band with a hairline, one leading glyph or none (severity on a confirmation, the subject's mark on a record, never a service tile), title at or under 20/28; blurred backdrop with a flat fallback under reduced transparency.
B17: a Platform page (core rule and crumbs); the connection and its dialog are identity; the DJDL Access row is license, the Console row core.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Pass. The kit's neutral dialog button now has a visible fill and hairline in dark; the dialog is centred and a bottom sheet on phone like the other turn-off dialogs.

findings.issue: Kit-wide: in dark the Cancel button had no visible fill or outline (same for 'Keep Diceroll' and sign-in-off's Cancel).
findings.resolution: Fixed in the kit (kit/mockup.css): in dark, a neutral .btn inside a dialog, drawer or popover takes --mk-fill-strong and a --pk-border-strong hairline. The page under the dialog was recomposed from identity.connection, so it carries that page's fixes; the dialog itself is unchanged apart from centring and the phone bottom sheet.

findings.issue: Title wrapped on phone; bullets of two clauses.
findings.resolution: Title 'Require SSO for this domain?'; bullets one clause each; background rebuilt on the new Connection layout; Cancel without focus fill.
